sentences.text: Hon'ble
Shri Justice Ravindra Kumar Agrawal Order on Board 12.09.2024 1.

This appeal under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicle Act, 1988 has been preferred by the appellants/Claimants, who are parents of the Mac 694 of 2017 deceased, challenging the award dated 25.01.2017 passed by the learned 2nd Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Korba,
District- Korba (for short, 'Claims Tribunal'), in Claim Case- 40 of 2015, whereby learned Claims Tribunal has awarded Rs.1,65,000/- as compensation to the claimants on account of death of the Smt. Pushpalata Sahu vs Devendra Kashyap on 12 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/80574099/
1 deceased boy-Ujwal Sahu, aged about two years.
2. The accident took place on 07.02.2015 by rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle, Car bearing No.CG-12 AG 2322 (hereafter, referred to as 'offending vehicle'), driven by NA1 Devendra Kashyap, owned by NA2 Smt I Baptishta, and was insured with NA3, Bajaj Alliance General Insurance Company Limited.
3. Claimants have filed the claim case for total amount of Rs.18 lakhs on various heads.
4.

entities.text: Bajaj Alliance General Insurance Company Limited
entities.label: RESPONDENT

sentences.text:
Learned counsel for the appellant would submit that the award passed by the learned Claims Tribunal is on lower side in view of decision passed by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the matter of Kurvan Ansari @ Kurvan Ali and another Vs Shyam Kishore Murmu and another, reported in (2022) 1 SCC 317, and Kishan Gopal and another Vs Lala and others reported in (2014) 1 SCC 244,
and further submits that the compensation amount awarded to the claimants may be enhanced suitably.

entities.text: Kurvan Ansari @ Kurvan Ali and another Vs Shyam Kishore Murmu and another, reported in (2022) 1 SCC 317
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Kishan Gopal and another Vs Lala and others reported in (2014) 1 SCC 244
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: On the other hand, learned counsel for respondent-3 Insurance Company opposed the submissions made by learned counsel for the appellants, and would submit that the learned Claims Tribunal has rightly passed the impugned award, which is strictly in accordance with law, and needs no interference by this court.

6. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
7.

Learned Claims Tribunal, considering the case of Lata Wadhwa and others Vs State of Bihar and others, reported in (2001) 8 SCC 197, has awarded Rs.1,50,000/- towards compensation, and Rs.15,000/- for funeral expenses, thus total Rs.1,65,000/- has been awarded to the claimants as compensation.

entities.text: Lata Wadhwa and others Vs State of Bihar and others, reported in (2001) 8 SCC 197
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 8. The legal principles laid down in cases of Kurvan Ansari and Kishan Gopal (supra), are applicable to the present case having regard to the fact that deceased is two years old child.

Taking the entire facts and circumstances of the case, and in view of above cases of Hon'ble Supreme court, this Court is of the opinion that ends of justice would meet by awarding lump-sum amount of Rs.5,00,000/- to the appellants/claimants.

9. Considering the entire facts and circumstances of the case, also considering that the deceased was aged about two years as per the post-mortem report, and Rs.5 lakhs as compensation would make it just and proper, therefore, the appeal is partly allowed.
Compensation Mac 694 of 2017 amount is enhanced to Rs.5,00,000/-.
After deducting Rs.1,65,000/-, which has already been awarded by the learned Claims Tribunal, appellants are now entitled for an additional amount of Rs.3,35,000/-, as compensation.
The enhanced amount of compensation shall carry interest @ 6% per annum from the date of claim application till its realization.

Smt. Pushpalata Sahu vs Devendra Kashyap on 12 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/80574099/
2 10.
The Insurance Company is directed to deposit the amount of compensation enhanced by this Court within a period of 60 days from today.

On such deposit being made by the Insurance Company, Rs.2,00,000/- (Rs.1,00,000/- each) shall be deposited in name of the claimants for a period of three years in fixed deposit in any nationalized bank, and the remaining amount shall be paid to the appellants/claimants through Bank transaction/Account payee cheque.
11. Appeal is partly allowed to the extent as indicated herein above.
12. No order as to costs.

Sd/-
(Ravindra Kumar Agrawal) JUDGE padma Smt. Pushpalata Sahu vs Devendra Kashyap on 12 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/80574099/
